nodes.description: Postzygotic activating missense mutations in GNAQ or GNA11 impair intrinsic guanosine triphosphatase (GTPase) hydrolysis of the Gαq/11 subunit, causing constitutive heterotrimeric G-protein signaling and downstream MAPK-family pathway activation in melanocyte lineages.

evidence.reference_title: Mosaic Activating Mutations in GNA11 and GNAQ Are Associated with Phakomatosis Pigmentovascularis and Extensive Dermal Melanocytosis.
evidence.snippet: Here, we discover that extensive dermal melanocytosis and phakomatosis pigmentovascularis are associated with activating mutations in GNA11 and GNAQ, genes that encode Gα subunits of heterotrimeric G proteins.

evidence.reference_title: Mosaic Activating Mutations in GNA11 and GNAQ Are Associated with Phakomatosis Pigmentovascularis and Extensive Dermal Melanocytosis.
evidence.snippet: Codon 183 in both GNA11 and GNAQ is located within the guanosine triphosphate binding region of the human Gα subunit, a region required for hydrolysis of guanosine triphosphate to guanosine diphosphate and an essential step for inactivation of G-protein coupled receptor signaling. Therefore, these mutations lead to decreased function of guanosine triphosphatase and to constitutive activation of downstream effector pathways.

evidence.reference_title: Mosaic Activating Mutations in GNA11 and GNAQ Are Associated with Phakomatosis Pigmentovascularis and Extensive Dermal Melanocytosis.
